name: 4-20 mA Signal Scaling
description: Converts a linear 4-20mA transmitter signal to an engineering value given the lower and upper range values.
variables: PV = process value, I = current signal (mA), LRV/URV = lower/upper range values
application: Any linear 4-20mA transmitter or I/O card scaling
assumptions: Linear transmitter response, no damping/offset error

name: Orifice Plate Flow
description: Volumetric flow rate through a square-edged concentric orifice plate.
variables: Q = flow, Cd = discharge coefficient, E = velocity of approach factor, d = bore, ΔP = differential pressure, ρ = density, β = d/D
application: Custody metering, process flow measurement
assumptions: Fully developed turbulent flow, square-edged plate, incompressible fluid

name: Liquid Valve Sizing (Cv)
description: Required flow coefficient for a control valve in non-flashing, non-cavitating liquid service.
variables: Cv = valve flow coefficient, Q = flow rate, ΔP = pressure drop, SG = specific gravity
application: Control valve preliminary sizing
assumptions: No flashing/cavitation, negligible piping geometry factor (Fp≈1)

name: Plant Heat Rate
description: Relates thermal efficiency to the fuel energy required per unit of electrical output.
variables: 860.42 = kcal equivalent of 1 kWh
application: Thermal power plant performance and fuel cost estimation
assumptions: Steady-state operation, efficiency includes boiler×turbine×generator

name: RTD Callendar-Van Dusen
description: Standard resistance-temperature relationship for platinum RTDs.
variables: R0 = resistance at 0°C, A = 3.9083e-3, B = -5.775e-7
application: Temperature measurement with Pt100/Pt1000 elements
assumptions: IEC 60751 class curve, negligible self-heating and lead-wire error

name: DP-Flow Square Root Relationship
description: Differential-pressure flow transmitters produce a signal proportional to the square of flow; extraction linearizes it.
variables: Flow% = percent of max flow, ΔP% = percent of max differential pressure
example: ΔP at 25% of span → Flow = √0.25 = 50% of max flow
application: Orifice/venturi/flow-nozzle DP flow measurement
assumptions: Beta ratio and fluid density constant across the range

name: Hydrostatic Pressure / Level
description: Pressure exerted by a column of liquid, used for level measurement via pressure/DP transmitters.
variables: P = pressure, ρ = fluid density, g = gravitational acceleration, h = liquid column height
application: Open/closed tank level measurement
assumptions: Constant density, static (no acceleration) column

name: PID Controller (parallel form)
formula: Output = Bias + Kp·e + Ki·∫e dt + Kd·de/dt
description: Standard parallel-form proportional-integral-derivative control law.
variables: e = SP−PV error, Kp/Ki/Kd = gains, Bias = output at zero error
application: Process control loop tuning and output prediction
assumptions: Linear control law, no output clamping/anti-windup modeled

name: Reynolds Number (pipe flow)
description: Dimensionless number indicating laminar vs turbulent flow regime.
variables: ṁ = mass flow rate, μ = dynamic viscosity, D = pipe internal diameter
application: Flow meter selection, discharge coefficient validity checks
assumptions: Fully developed, Newtonian fluid

name: Pump Head & Hydraulic Power
description: Shaft power required to deliver a given flow against a given head at a stated pump efficiency.
variables: ρ = density, Q = flow (m3/s), H = head (m), η = pump efficiency (fraction)
application: Pump selection and motor sizing
assumptions: Constant density, steady flow, efficiency includes hydraulic+mechanical losses

name: Simply Supported Beam Deflection (Point Load)
description: Maximum deflection of a simply supported beam under a center point load, classical Euler-Bernoulli beam theory.
variables: δ_max = max deflection, P = point load, L = span, E = modulus of elasticity, I = moment of inertia
units: N, m, Pa, m⁴ → result in m
application: Simply supported beam design and deflection serviceability check
assumptions: Linear elastic material, small deflections, uniform cross-section
standard: Classical mechanics of materials (Euler-Bernoulli beam theory)

name: Euler Column Buckling
description: Elastic critical buckling load for a slender column, for any standard end-support condition via the effective length factor K.
variables: P_cr = critical load, E = modulus of elasticity, I = moment of inertia, K = effective length factor, L = unsupported length
units: Pa, m⁴, m → result in N
application: Preliminary column buckling check
assumptions: Perfectly elastic, initially straight, centrally loaded column — no safety factor included

name: Concrete Nominal Mix Quantities
formula: Material volume = Dry volume × (ratio part / sum of ratio parts)
description: Cement, sand and aggregate quantities for an IS 456:2000 nominal concrete mix, using the standard 1.54 dry volume factor.
variables: Dry volume = wet volume × 1.54 (typical), ratio = fixed cement:sand:aggregate proportion by grade
example: M20 (1:1.5:3), 1 m³ wet volume → dry volume 1.54 m³ → cement = 1.54×(1/5.5) = 0.28 m³ → ×1440 kg/m³ / 50 kg/bag ≈ 8.06 bags
application: Material quantity estimation for ordinary grade concrete (M5–M20)
assumptions: IS 456:2000 nominal mix method; M25 and above require a design mix, not covered by this method

name: Rebar (Reinforcement Bar) Weight
formula: W = ρ × (πd²/4) × L  (site rule of thumb: W/L ≈ d²/162 kg/m)
description: Weight of a rebar/reinforcement bar from its diameter and length, using steel density; the familiar d²/162 site approximation gives the same result within about 0.1%.
variables: W = weight, ρ = steel density (7850 kg/m³), d = bar diameter (mm), L = length (m)
example: 16 mm bar, 1 m long → W = 7850 × (π×0.016²/4) × 1 = 1.578 kg (rule of thumb 16²/162 = 1.580 kg)
application: Reinforcement material takeoff and procurement
assumptions: Standard steel density 7850 kg/m³

name: Rankine Active Earth Pressure
description: Active earth pressure coefficient and pressure on a retaining wall from Rankine theory, for a cohesionless or cohesive soil.
variables: Kₐ = active pressure coefficient, φ = soil friction angle, σv = vertical (overburden) stress, c = cohesion
application: Retaining wall design, preliminary lateral earth pressure estimate
assumptions: Vertical wall face, horizontal backfill, no wall friction (real design should also check Coulomb theory)

name: Manning's Equation (Open Channel Flow)
description: Mean flow velocity in an open channel under uniform flow conditions, from the channel's roughness, hydraulic radius, and slope.
variables: V = velocity, n = Manning's roughness coefficient, R = hydraulic radius (A/P), S = longitudinal channel slope
example: Rectangular channel, b=2 m, depth=1 m, n=0.013, S=0.001 → A=2 m², P=4 m, R=0.5 m → V=1.53 m/s, Q=3.06 m³/s
application: Open channel and storm drain flow capacity calculations
assumptions: Uniform (steady, normal) flow, constant cross-section and slope

name: Effective Stress (Terzaghi)
description: Effective stress carried by the soil skeleton, equal to total stress minus pore water pressure — the fundamental principle underlying settlement, bearing capacity, and slope stability analysis.
variables: σ' = effective stress, σ = total stress (from soil self-weight), u = pore water pressure
example: Depth 5 m, water table at 2 m, γ(above)=17, γ(below)=19 kN/m³ → σ=17×2+19×3=91 kPa, u=9.81×3=29.43 kPa → σ'=61.57 kPa
application: Foundation settlement and bearing capacity analysis
assumptions: Hydrostatic pore pressure (no seepage flow)

name: Pump Specific Speed
description: Dimensional specific speed used to indicate centrifugal pump impeller geometry family (radial, mixed, or axial flow) at a given duty point.
variables: Ns = specific speed, N = pump speed (rpm), Q = flow at best efficiency point (US gpm), H = head per stage (ft)
example: N=1770 rpm, Q=500 gpm, H=150 ft → Ns = 1770√500/150^0.75 ≈ 923 (radial flow range)
application: Early-stage pump type / impeller family selection
assumptions: US customary unit form; numerically different in other unit systems for the same physical pump

name: HVAC Sensible Heat Load
description: Standard ASHRAE air-side sensible heat formula, relating airflow and temperature change to cooling or heating load.
variables: Q = sensible heat load, CFM/L⁄s = airflow, ΔT = temperature difference across the coil or space
application: HVAC sensible cooling/heating load estimation
assumptions: Sensible heat only — excludes latent (moisture) load, solar gain, occupancy and infiltration

name: Bolt Torque-Tension Relationship
description: Standard fastener torque-tension relationship relating tightening torque to target clamp force via the nut factor K.
variables: T = tightening torque, K = nut factor (lubrication/thread condition dependent, typically 0.10–0.20), D = bolt diameter, F = target clamp force
application: Bolted joint tightening specification
assumptions: K is not universal — varies with lubrication and plating; use the bolt's own datasheet value where available
standard: Shigley's Mechanical Engineering Design; standard fastener engineering practice

name: Refrigeration Ton Conversion
description: Standard definition of a ton of refrigeration, used throughout HVAC and refrigeration capacity ratings.
variables: Defined from the latent heat to freeze one short ton of 0°C water to ice in 24 hours
application: Converting between chiller/AC capacity units
assumptions: Exact definitional constant, not an approximation

name: Duct Sizing (Velocity Method)
description: Required duct cross-sectional area and equivalent round-duct diameter from airflow and a chosen design velocity.
variables: Area = required duct cross-section, Flow = airflow (CFM or L/s), Velocity = target design velocity
example: 2000 CFM at 1000 fpm → Area = 2 ft² → round duct diameter ≈ 19.1 in
application: Sizing a single HVAC duct section for a target velocity
assumptions: Target velocity is a design choice (noise/pressure-drop trade-off), not a fixed physical constant

name: Gear Ratio (Speed and Torque)
description: Ideal kinematic relationship between gear tooth counts, rotational speed, and torque across a gear mesh.
variables: N = rotational speed, D = pitch diameter (or tooth count), T = torque; subscripts 1=driving gear, 2=driven gear
example: 1800 rpm input, 20 teeth driving 60 teeth → ratio 3:1 → output speed 600 rpm
application: Gearbox/gear train speed and torque calculation
assumptions: Ideal kinematic relationship — real torque output is reduced by mesh efficiency losses

name: Belt and Pulley Speed Ratio
description: Exact kinematic relationship between belt-driven pulley diameters and rotational speeds, assuming no belt slip.
variables: N = rotational speed, D = pulley diameter; subscripts 1=driving pulley, 2=driven pulley
example: 1450 rpm motor with 100 mm pulley driving a 250 mm pulley → output speed = 1450×100/250 = 580 rpm
application: Belt drive speed reduction/increase calculation
assumptions: No belt slip — real belts under heavy load can slip slightly, reducing actual output speed below this ideal value

name: SAMA Logic Blocks (Summer, Select, Limit, AND/OR)
formula: Summer: out = Σ(gain_i × input_i) + bias   High/Low Select: out = max/min(inputs)
description: Standard SAMA (Scientific Apparatus Makers Association) function blocks used throughout combustion and boiler control interlock/permissive logic diagrams.
variables: Summer: weighted sum plus bias; High/Low Select: outputs the highest/lowest input; Limiters clamp output to a bound; AND/OR/NOT are standard boolean logic (>=0.5 treated as TRUE)
units: Engineering units of the signal being summed/selected/limited; dimensionless for logic blocks
example: High Select of fuel demand (70%) and air feedforward (65%) → output = max(70,65) = 70%, the standard cross-limiting air floor
application: Building and simulating custom interlock/permissive control logic from standard symbols
assumptions: Static/algebraic blocks only — no dynamic (lag, integrator, timer) blocks, which need time-stepped simulation instead
standard: SAMA (Scientific Apparatus Makers Association) PMC 22.1 standard symbols
